messages:
jia: Heads-up — onboarding llama5 via mistral-bridge with int4 quant. Seeing a consistent summarization quality drop vs float32 baseline on news-sum and conversational QA tests. Repro steps below.

jia: Repro (local):
```
# convert + quant
python tools/convert_model.py --src=llama5 --target=mistral-bridge --out=llama5-mb/ --quant=ptq-int4 --group-size=128
# run eval harness
./eval/harness --model ./llama5-mb/ --task news-sum --seed 42 --batch 8
```

oliver: How big is the drop? any scalar metrics?

jia: Rouge-L down ~5 pts, BLEU -2, qualitative: short hallucinations in ~12% of outputs (was ~2% baseline). Perplexity on eval set +0.55. Unit tests / logits-check scripts don't crash.

sam: Which quant config exactly? per-channel or per-tensor? symmetric or asymmetric?

jia: Per-channel symmetric, group-size=128, no clamp. Used gemma-quant-v2 tool with our ml-convert wrapper. No fudge on rotary params during conversion.

natalie: Could be rotary frequency/scale mismatch after bridge conversion — Llama5 uses slightly different head ordering and rope scaling compared to older Llama variants. Also check vocab offset mapping (we recently saw a +1 EOS shift for a different model).

jia: Agreed. I diffed a single-layer attention scale vs float32: head 7 shows angle scale ~1.0008 vs 1.0 and logits for some tokens shift noticeably. KV cache offsets look OK for first 64 tokens though.

oliver: Can you run a logits ddiff for first 128 tokens between float32 and int4 (same seed) and show top-5 token diffs per step? that will tell us if it's angle/rotary or a projection reorder.

jia: Starting a job now. Command:
```
./tools/logit_ddiff --float ./models/llama5-fp32 --quant ./llama5-mb/ --seq-len 128 --out /tmp/ddiff.json
```

ci-bot: Job queued: 9500001234-ci-quant-audit. Will post results here when done.

sam: Also run conversion with group-size=64 and per-tensor as a quick ablation. If quality improves with smaller group, it's quant granularity. If not, look at rotary/key ordering.

ci-bot: Job finished: 9500001234-ci-quant-audit. Summary: ddiff shows large per-step divergence starting at token 12; top-5 mismatch rate increases from 3% -> 18% by token 40. Head-level breakdown: head 7 and 11 have highest L2 diff. Angle scaling factor measured ~1.0008 on those heads.

natalie: That angle scale delta is tiny but consistent — we've seen tiny rotary scale offsets amplify over autoregressive steps. Suggest test: after conversion multiply rotary angles by 0.9992 (inverse factor) and rerun eval.

jia: Running that patch now (quick hack in conversion layer to adjust inv_freq). Also spinning up ablations: group-size [64,128,256], per-channel vs per-tensor, and conversion variant that reorders head dims with our headmap shim.

oliver: If rotary tweak fixes most regression, we should add an automated check to conversion pipeline: compute per-head rotary scale and reject conversions where any head deviates >5e-4.

sam: Agreed. Also add a small token-level smoke eval (10 examples from news-sum) to CI for new converts.

ci-bot: Patch-run finished: rotary rescale 0.9992 reduced Rouge-L gap to ~1.2 pts and hallucination rate down to ~4%. Group-size=64 per-channel also helps but not as much as rotary fix.

natalie: Nice. Plan: 1) add rotary-scale sanity check and auto-correct option in converter, 2) run full eval suite across quant configs, 3) open ticket with triage steps and assign to sam+jia. I'll create MLD-3421.

jia: Created MLD-3421: "llama5->mistral-bridge int4: rotary-scale mismatch causing quality regression". Added links to ddiff output and eval artifacts.

oliver: For record — root cause hypothesis: conversion omitted a model-specific rotary normalization constant (small factor) that cascades in autoregressive decoding. Fixes: auto-detect & adjust or embed shim mapping in conversion.

sam: I'll follow up with a PR for the converter tests and add the small smoke eval in CI. ETA EOD tomorrow.

natalie: Thanks everyone. If CI shows anything unexpected, tag #eng-ml and ping me. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: Closing job 9500001234-ci-quant-audit (artifacts uploaded: /ci/artifacts/9500001234/).
